body:
What is d/dx[csc x cot x]?

Choices:
A. csc x(csc²x − cot²x)
B. −cot x(csc²x + cot²x)
C. csc x(cot²x + csc²x)
D. −csc x(cot²x + csc²x)

What is d/dx[x² sec x]?

Choices:
A. x sec x(2 + tan x)
B. 2x sec x tan x
C. x sec x(2 − x tan x)
D. x sec x(2 + x tan x)

A 90% confidence interval for a population proportion, based on a random sample of 400 voters, has a margin of error of 0.04. If the pollsters instead sampled 1600 voters, with the same confidence level and about the same sample proportion, what would the margin of error be approximately?

Choices:
A. 0.02
B. 0.04
C. 0.01
D. 0.08

A poll of 500 randomly chosen adults gives a 90% confidence interval for a population proportion. If the pollster keeps the same data but reports a 99% confidence interval, what happens to the margin of error?

Choices:
A. It gets larger, because the critical value z* increases from about 1.645 to about 2.576.
B. It stays the same, because the standard error depends only on n and p̂.
C. It gets smaller, because greater confidence means a more precise estimate.
D. It gets larger, because 99% confidence needs a larger sample.

A researcher wants a 95% confidence interval for a population proportion with a margin of error no larger than 0.03, and has no prior estimate of the proportion. Using z* = 1.96 and the most conservative p̂ = 0.5, what is the minimum sample size?

Choices:
A. 278
B. 545
C. 1068
D. 1067

Red blood cells contain aquaporin-1 (AQP1) channels. When wild-type red blood cells are moved into a hypotonic solution, they swell and lyse in about 20 seconds. Red blood cells from mice lacking AQP1 also swell and lyse in the same solution, but only after about 60 seconds, which is 3 times as long as the wild type. The solutions and internal osmolarities are identical in both groups. Which explanation best accounts for the difference?

Choices:
A. Without AQP1, water still crosses by diffusing through the phospholipid bilayer, but more slowly, so the cells swell and lyse after a longer time.
B. AQP1 channels use ATP to push water into the cell, so cells lacking them have less energy to draw in water.
C. The knockout cells have a lower internal solute concentration, so the osmotic gradient is smaller and swelling is slower.
D. Without AQP1, water cannot cross the plasma membrane, so the knockout cells swell only because solutes enter them over time.
